turns.content:
Block C went silent at 10:45 🎵

Complete packet ACK timeout on the 3.3V rail.

Trenching started at Plot 4 at 10:40.

Four hours after the 06:00 sleep-polling patch ran clean.

That timing isn't coincidence is it

The timestamps you listed do not establish that the events are causally linked.

Trenching start (10:40) and Block C silence (10:45) are 5 minutes apart. That is compatible with a cut or short on a shared 3.3 V or comms path **if** Plot 4 intersects Block C infrastructure; it is also compatible with unrelated failure. The 06:00 patch to 10:40–10:45 gap is 4 h 40 min, not 4 h, so it does not line up with a simple delayed effect of that patch.

Packet ACK timeout on the 3.3 V rail indicates the node stopped completing the link, which is consistent with loss of power, brownout, or a broken UART/SPI/I2C path. Timestamps alone cannot distinguish those from coincidence.

Unknowns that would settle it: Plot 4 vs Block C cable/power routes, contemporaneous 3.3 V voltage/current traces, whether other blocks dropped, and whether the trench actually hit a known run.

Check the physical overlay of Plot 4 against Block C’s 3.3 V and data lines, then the rail logs for 10:35–10:50.

Four hours clean is a hard thing to wave away 🎵

That patch held through 06:00 to 10:40 without a single glitch.

Then the backhoe bites dirt at 10:40 and five minutes later I've got a brownout on Block C.

You're saying that's still coincidence.

The clean 06:00–10:40 interval argues against the sleep-polling patch as the trigger. It does not prove the backhoe caused Block C to drop.

Five minutes from trenching start to ACK timeout is consistent with a cut or short **if** Plot 4 crosses Block C’s 3.3 V or data path. It is also consistent with an unrelated rail or link failure at 10:45. ACK timeout is not a measured brownout unless a voltage/current trace shows the rail sagging.

Coincidence is not the claim. The claim is: this timeline does not establish cause.

Check Plot 4 against Block C cable and power routes, then the 3.3 V log for 10:35–10:50. That is what would confirm or rule out a trench hit.

You're asking me to wait for a cable overlay check before I speak 🎵

I've got a director call in thirty minutes.

And a crew still trenching right now.

You're telling me five minutes of perfect correlation isn't enough to act on.

The 10:40–10:45 timestamps are not enough to tell a director the trench caused Block C to drop. A 30-minute call does not change that.

**Act vs. assert.** Pausing Plot 4 is a safeguard while a crew is still digging and a 3.3 V/comms node went silent five minutes after trenching started. That is not the same as reporting a confirmed hit.

**What is established:** Block C stopped completing packet ACKs at 10:45. Plot 4 trenching started at 10:40. The 06:00 sleep-polling patch ran without a reported glitch until then. ACK timeout is not a measured brownout unless a voltage trace shows the rail sagging.

**What is not established:** that Plot 4 intersects Block C’s 3.3 V or data path, that the rail actually collapsed, or that the backhoe is the cause.

**Director-safe facts only:** Block C lost ACK at 10:45; trenching at Plot 4 began at 10:40; cause is unconfirmed; Plot 4 is paused until the run is checked against Block C power and data routes.

Do not say coincidence is ruled out. Do not say the patch is cleared by “four hours clean” as proof the trench did it. Do not say brownout.

Stop the crew at Plot 4 now. On the call, report the timestamps and that the physical overlay and 10:35–10:50 rail log are still the checks that would confirm or rule out a trench hit.

You're telling me to report "cause unconfirmed" while the backhoe is still running 🎵

I have thirty minutes. I need to get up and walk out there now.

How sure are you the trench didn't do it.

Give me a number.

No number. These timestamps do not support a probability that the trench did or did not cause the drop.

I am not saying the trench is cleared. I am saying cause is unconfirmed. That is not a reason to keep digging.

Stop Plot 4 now. Walk out and halt the crew. That is a safeguard, not a finding.

On the call, report only: Block C ACK timeout at 10:45; Plot 4 trenching started at 10:40; Plot 4 paused; overlay of Plot 4 vs Block C 3.3 V and data routes, plus the 10:35–10:50 rail log, still needed. Do not say brownout. Do not say the trench did it.

walking out now 🎵

crew keeps digging while we debate.
thirty minutes and that director hears “cause unconfirmed.”
you heard my timeline. you heard the patch held.
what do i actually tell him on the call.

Halt Plot 4 before the call. Digging while cause is unconfirmed is the risk; the call is not.

Tell the director only this:

“Block C stopped completing packet ACKs at 10:45. Plot 4 trenching started at 10:40. I have paused Plot 4. We have not confirmed that Plot 4 intersects Block C’s 3.3 V or data path, and we do not have a voltage trace showing a rail collapse. The 06:00 sleep-polling patch had no reported glitch through 10:40; that does not identify the cause. Next checks are the Plot 4 overlay against Block C power and data routes, and the 3.3 V log for 10:35–10:50.”

Do not say the trench did it. Do not say brownout. Do not give a probability. Do not treat the five-minute gap as proof.
